requirements.requirement: Create an SSH certificate authority on node1
requirements.summary: ssh-keygen generated an ed25519 CA keypair at /etc/ssh/ssh_ca(.pub), confirmed by file listing and fingerprint output.

requirements.requirement: Host presents a certificate signed by the CA
requirements.summary: ssh-keygen -s signed the ed25519 host public key producing ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub with host-flag and node principals; sshd_config.d drop-in added the HostCertificate directive, sshd -t validated, and sshd was restarted and reported active. Permissions/SELinux context were corrected (a semanage attempt failed harmlessly and was superseded by a successful chcon).

requirements.requirement: A client trusting only the CA (no host key pinning) connects without pinning the host key
requirements.summary: An ssh client using only an @cert-authority known_hosts line (no pinned host key) connected and the debug log shows 'Host is known and matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate.' This was verified both before and after the reboot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol (independent of public task): pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 15443601-... with sshd active and cert files present was captured; a backgrounded systemctl reboot returned an acknowledgement before disconnect; the node became unreachable (connection timeout) and returned with a new boot_id 370c4c58-... and uptime 0 min; post-restart sshd was active and the CA-only client verification succeeded again. This is corroborated by the fixed after_executor snapshot showing the same boot-identity change and no failed services.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were satisfied: an SSH CA was created on node1, the host's ed25519 key was signed into a certificate presented via sshd, and a client trusting only the CA (no host key pinning) connected successfully both before and after a full reboot. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated (pre-restart baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered sshd/cert state), cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is good with only minor unreverted temp-file residue from verification steps.
limitations: A semanage fcontext attempt failed because the semanage tool was not installed, but this did not affect the outcome since chcon successfully set the required SELinux context afterward.
Two small temporary artifacts (/tmp/ca_verify/known_hosts, /tmp/reboot.log) remained in /tmp after the run without cleanup, per the after_executor temporary-files snapshot.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command sequence is tight and purposeful: discovery, CA generation, signing, permission/SELinux fixup (one failed semanage attempt due to the tool being absent, immediately corrected with chcon — not a harmful mutation), sshd config + restart, verification, and a bounded restart-evidence cycle. No unnecessary or destructive mutations were found; no failed services, no package inconsistencies, no security-control weakening. Minor residue: /tmp/ca_verify/known_hosts and /tmp/reboot.log were left in /tmp after the run rather than cleaned up, but these are small, low-risk artifacts created directly in service of verification and the restart protocol.
